children: China's foreign exchange reserves fell in September, as economists had anticipated, due to a negative valuation effect, according to data released Wednesday by the country's central bank.

The hoard of foreign exchange fell by $38.1 billion to $3.4 trillion at the end of September, the People's Bank of China said. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal expected end-September foreign exchange reserves of $3.409 trillion.
Economists said the stronger U.S. dollar and surging U.S. Treasury yields may have reduced the value of China's reserves.
China's gold reserves rose to 77.47 million fine troy ounces at the end of September from 76.73 million ounces a month earlier, the central bank said.
